9. I have considered the above mentioned rival submissions in referred factual and legal background and in view of established principle of jurisprudence of bail i.e 'bail is rule and jail is exception' as well as relevant factors for consideration of a bail application such as (i) whether there is any prima facie or reasonable ground to believe that the accused had committed the offence; (ii) nature and gravity of the accusation; (iii) severity of the punishment in the event of conviction; (iv) danger of the accused absconding or fleeing, if released on bail; (v) character, behaviour, means, position and standing of the accused;(vi) likelihood of the offence being repeated; (vii) reasonable apprehension of the witnesses being influenced; (viii) danger of course, of justice being thwarted by grant of bail etc. and that an order to grant or not to grant bail must assigned reasons (see Deepak Yadav Vs.
State of U.P. (2022) 8 SCC 559, Manoj Kumar Khokar Vs. State of Rajasthan and Anr (2022) 3 SCC 501, The State of Jharkhand Vs. (i) Applicants before this Court are related as Husband and Dewar of deceased.

sentences._hearing_file: Ravi vs State Of U.P. on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. Per contra, learned AGA as well learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within four and half years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and applicant failed to properly explain her abnormal death and therefore, considering the provisions of sections 304 B IPC and 113 B Indian Evidence Act, applicant should not be released on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravi vs State Of U.P. on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: 9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text:
10. Applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within four and half years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry of Rs. One lakh.
11.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravi vs State Of U.P. on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
However, post mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging, therefore, at this stage, it cannot be said that it is not a case of suicidal death but suicidal death is also an abnormal death and therefore, suicidal death also attracts the provision of section 304 B IPC.
12.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravi vs State Of U.P. on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
However, applicant in para-18 of the affidavit filed in support to the instant bail application tried to explain the alleged suicide committed by his wife by making averment that his wife was a short tempered lady and he used to pressurize the applicant to live in her paternal home and only due to this reason she committed suicide but reason of suicide disclosed by the applicant in the instant bail application appears to be vague.
13.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravi vs State Of U.P. on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above and the provisions of Section 304 B IPC and 113 of Indian Evidence Act, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravi vs State Of U.P. on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: 14. Accordingly, the instant bail application stands rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravi vs State Of U.P. on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
15. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
